:::{#thm-kl-divergence-discrete}
#### KL divergence of two mass functions

Let $p$ and $q$ be [probability mass functions](random-variables.qmd#def-pmf) on $\set{1, \ldots, K}$,
with $p_k$ and $q_k$ the probabilities of [outcome](#def-outcome) $k$,
and suppose $q_k > 0$
whenever $p_k > 0$.
Then the [KL divergence](#def-kl-divergence) is

$$\kldivf{p}{q} = \sumto{k}{K} p_k \log \frac{p_k}{q_k}.$$

A term with $p_k = 0$ is taken to be $0$.

:::

::: proof

Let $X$ have [mass function](random-variables.qmd#def-pmf) $p$,
and let $g(k) \eqdef -\log q_k + \log p_k$ for each $k$ with $p_k > 0$,
so that $\surprisalunderf{q}{X} - \surprisalunderf{p}{X} = g(X)$.
Since $q_k > 0$ whenever $p_k > 0$,
$g(k)$ is a real number for every value $k$ that $X$ takes with positive [probability](probability-basics.qmd#def-probability).
By [LOTUS](#thm-lotus),

$$
\ba
\kldivf{p}{q}
&= \E{g(X)} && \text{(definition)} \\
&= \sum_{k : p_k > 0} g(k) \cd \P(X = k) && \text{(LOTUS)} \\
&= \sum_{k : p_k > 0} p_k \paren{\log p_k - \log q_k} && \text{(definition of } g \text{ and } \P(X = k) = p_k \text{)} \\
&= \sum_{k : p_k > 0} p_k \log \frac{p_k}{q_k} && \text{(difference of logarithms)} \\
&= \sumto{k}{K} p_k \log \frac{p_k}{q_k}. && \text{(terms with } p_k = 0 \text{ are } 0 \text{)}
\ea
$$

:::
